subproblem.title: Fatou lower bound for integrals from the liminf inequality on bounded open sets
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (Measure (Euclid P)). Assume μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) (in [0, ∞]) for every bounded open set G ⊆ ℝ^P. Then for every continuous g : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and g(x) ≥ 0 for all x, ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ_j, where ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral with values in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → Bornology.IsBounded G → μ G ≤ liminf (fun j => μs j G) atTop) → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) → ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (g x) ∂μ ≤ liminf (fun j => ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (g x) ∂(μs j)) atTop
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 and 4 of the supplied proof of `dtc_bc_tendsto_integral_of_limsup_liminf` (the 'standard approximation argument' that ends Simon's proof of 7.2.4, chapter-07.txt lines 285–288), stated for one nonnegative function g. Only the bounded-open-set hypothesis is used; no finiteness assumption is needed. This is the open-set half of the portmanteau theorem: Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.lintegral_le_liminf_lintegral_of_forall_isOpen_measure_le_liminf_measure` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Portmanteau.lean) has the same proof but assumes the inequality for all open sets and is outside the import closure of `GMT.Ch07.Submission`; here only bounded open sets occur.
Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support and g(x) ≥ 0 for all x. Write K₀ := tsupport g = closure{x : g(x) ≠ 0} and, for t ∈ ℝ, G_t := {x : t < g(x)}.
1. (K₀ is bounded.) Since g has compact support, K₀ is compact (`HasCompactSupport.isCompact`), hence bounded in the metric space ℝ^P (`IsCompact.isBounded`).
2. (Layer cake.) Let ν be any measure on ℝ^P (σ-finiteness is not needed: the cited lemma assumes only a.e. nonnegativity and a.e. measurability). Since g ≥ 0 everywhere and g is continuous, hence Borel measurable, the layer cake formula with strict superlevel sets gives ∫⁻ ofReal(g(x)) dν(x) = ∫⁻_{t∈(0,∞)} ν(G_t) dt, the outer integral being taken against Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞) (`lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt ν (ae_of_all _ hg0) hg.measurable.aemeasurable`). We use this for ν = μ and for ν = μ_j, every j.
3. (For t > 0, G_t is bounded and open.) Let t > 0. G_t = g⁻¹((t, ∞)) is open because g is continuous (`isOpen_lt continuous_const hg`). If x ∈ G_t then g(x) > t > 0, so g(x) ≠ 0 and x ∈ support g ⊆ K₀ (`subset_tsupport`). Hence G_t ⊆ K₀, so G_t is bounded by step 1 (`Bornology.IsBounded.subset`). By the hypothesis, μ(G_t) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G_t) for every t > 0.
4. (Measurability.) For j ∈ ℕ and t ∈ ℝ put F_j(t) := μ_j(G_t). If s ≤ t then t < g(x) implies s < g(x), so G_t ⊆ G_s and F_j(t) ≤ F_j(s) (`measure_mono`). Thus F_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] is antitone, hence Borel measurable (`Antitone.measurable`).
5. (Integrating the pointwise inequality.) By step 3, μ(G_t) ≤ liminf_j F_j(t) for every t in the measurable set (0, ∞). Monotonicity of the integral over (0, ∞) gives ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ(G_t) dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} liminf_j F_j(t) dt (`setLIntegral_mono' measurableSet_Ioi`).
6. (Fatou.) Fatou's lemma for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞), applied to the measurable functions F_j of step 4 (`lintegral_liminf_le`), gives ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} liminf_j F_j(t) dt ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} F_j(t) dt.
7. (Conclusion.) By step 2 for ν = μ, steps 5 and 6, and step 2 for ν = μ_j:
   ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ(G_t) dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} liminf_j F_j(t) dt ≤ liminf_j ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} F_j(t) dt = liminf_j ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ_j. ∎
proof_key_steps: Layer cake with strict superlevel sets: ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dν = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ν({g > t}) dt for ν = μ and ν = μ_j.
For t > 0, {g > t} is open and contained in the compact set tsupport g, hence bounded, so μ({g > t}) ≤ liminf_j μ_j({g > t}).
t ↦ μ_j({g > t}) is antitone, hence measurable.
Integrate the pointwise inequality over (0, ∞) and apply Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le).

No finiteness assumption or circular reliance is hidden, and the proof is ready for formalization.

subproblem.title: Reverse-Fatou upper bound for integrals from the limsup inequality on compact sets
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (Measure (Euclid P)). Assume (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) (in [0, ∞]) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. Then for every continuous g : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and g(x) ≥ 0 for all x, limsup_j ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ_j ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ, where ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral with values in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K) → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) → limsup (fun j => ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (g x) ∂(μs j)) atTop ≤ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (g x) ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the eventual bound of step 1 and steps 3 and 5 of the supplied proof of `dtc_bc_tendsto_integral_of_limsup_liminf` (the 'standard approximation argument' that ends Simon's proof of 7.2.4, chapter-07.txt lines 285–288), stated for one nonnegative function g. The bounded-open-set hypothesis is not used. Hypothesis (a) is used only for K₀ = tsupport g (step 2) and cannot be dropped: on ℝ¹, μ = ∞·δ₀, μ_n = n²·δ_{1/n} and g(x) = max(0, x(1 − x)) satisfy (b), yet ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ_n = n − 1 → ∞ while ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ = 0.
Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support and g(x) ≥ 0 for all x. Write K₀ := tsupport g and, for t ∈ ℝ, C_t := {x : t ≤ g(x)}.
1. (Bound for g.) K₀ is compact (`HasCompactSupport.isCompact`). A continuous function with compact support is bounded: there is M ∈ ℝ with ‖g(x)‖ ≤ M for all x (`Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support`), hence g(x) ≤ ‖g(x)‖ ≤ M for all x (`Real.le_norm_self`).
2. (Eventual bound on μ_j(K₀).) By (a), μ(K₀) < ∞. Put A := μ(K₀) + 1. Then A < ∞ and μ(K₀) < A (`ENNReal.lt_add_right`). By (b), limsup_j μ_j(K₀) ≤ μ(K₀) < A, so μ_j(K₀) < A for all sufficiently large j (`eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt`; its boundedness side condition holds automatically in [0, ∞]). Fix j₁ ∈ ℕ with μ_j(K₀) < A for every j ≥ j₁ (`eventually_atTop`).
3. (Superlevel sets.) Let t > 0. If x ∈ C_t then g(x) ≥ t > 0, so g(x) ≠ 0 and x ∈ support g ⊆ K₀ (`subset_tsupport`); thus C_t ⊆ K₀. Since g is continuous, C_t = g⁻¹([t, ∞)) is closed (`isClosed_le continuous_const hg`), so C_t is compact as a closed subset of the compact set K₀ (`IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset`). If t > M then C_t = ∅, because g(x) ≤ M < t for every x.
4. (Layer cake.) For every measure ν on ℝ^P (σ-finiteness is not needed: the cited lemma assumes only a.e. nonnegativity and a.e. measurability), since g ≥ 0 is continuous, hence Borel measurable, the layer cake formula with closed superlevel sets gives ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dν = ∫⁻_{t∈(0,∞)} ν(C_t) dt, against Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞) (`lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le ν (ae_of_all _ hg0) hg.measurable.aemeasurable`).
5. (Index shift.) For every sequence (a_j) in [0, ∞], limsup_j a_j = limsup_i a_{i+j₁} (`limsup_nat_add`). For i ∈ ℕ and t ∈ ℝ put G_i(t) := μ_{i+j₁}(C_t).
6. (Measurability.) If s ≤ t then C_t ⊆ C_s, so G_i(t) ≤ G_i(s) (`measure_mono`). Thus each G_i : ℝ → [0, ∞] is antitone, hence Borel measurable (`Antitone.measurable`).
7. (Domination.) Let D := A·1_{(−∞, M]}, i.e. D(t) = A for t ≤ M and D(t) = 0 for t > M. Fix i ∈ ℕ and t > 0. If t ≤ M, then by step 3 and step 2 (note i + j₁ ≥ j₁), G_i(t) ≤ μ_{i+j₁}(K₀) < A = D(t). If t > M, then C_t = ∅ by step 3, so G_i(t) = 0 ≤ D(t). Hence G_i ≤ D almost everywhere for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞) (`ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioi`). Moreover ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} D dt = A · Leb((−∞, M] ∩ (0, ∞)) = A · Leb((0, M]) = A · ofReal(M − 0) < ∞ (`lintegral_indicator measurableSet_Iic`, `setLIntegral_const`, `Measure.restrict_apply measurableSet_Iic`, `Iic_inter_Ioi`, `Real.volume_Ioc`, `ENNReal.mul_ne_top`).
8. (Reverse Fatou.) The reverse Fatou lemma for Lebesgue measure restricted to (0, ∞), applied to the measurable functions G_i of step 6 with the dominating function D of step 7 (`limsup_lintegral_le D hmeas hbound hfin`), gives limsup_i ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} G_i(t) dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} limsup_i G_i(t) dt.
9. (Pointwise bound.) Let t > 0. By step 5, limsup_i G_i(t) = limsup_j μ_j(C_t), and limsup_j μ_j(C_t) ≤ μ(C_t) by (b), because C_t is compact (step 3). Hence ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} limsup_i G_i(t) dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ(C_t) dt (`setLIntegral_mono' measurableSet_Ioi`).
10. (Conclusion.) By step 4 for ν = μ_j, step 5, step 8, step 9 and step 4 for ν = μ:
    limsup_j ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ_j = limsup_j ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ_j(C_t) dt = limsup_i ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} G_i(t) dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} limsup_i G_i(t) dt ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ(C_t) dt = ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dμ. ∎
proof_key_steps: g ≤ M; by (a) and (b) fix j₁ with μ_j(tsupport g) < A := μ(tsupport g) + 1 < ∞ for all j ≥ j₁.
For t > 0, {g ≥ t} is a closed subset of tsupport g, hence compact, and it is empty for t > M.
Layer cake with closed superlevel sets, then shift the index by j₁ (limsup_nat_add).
G_i(t) = μ_{i+j₁}({g ≥ t}) is antitone, hence measurable, and dominated on (0, ∞) by A·1_{(−∞,M]}, whose integral is finite.
Reverse Fatou (limsup_lintegral_le), then (b) on the compact sets {g ≥ t} pointwise, then layer cake for μ.

Compact finiteness and the limsup bound supply a finite uniform bound after an index shift. Positive closed superlevels are compact, and the indicator majorant has finite integral on (0,∞). Measurability, reverse Fatou, tail invariance, and layer cake then prove the exact conclusion. All side conditions are supplied; the proof is complete and non-circular.
